**Security: block**, round-two delta at `26d2df93dba7bb02dbaf7829928875c52d8961b3`, against `703cde7710d62080907527de0e426e3d2fbe5c26` (migration 0046).

The conflicting-FYI false-Held response is repaired, with transactional refusal/audit. S189-001 is not fully closed: the new shared random occurrence becomes observable before the prime's FYI is admitted, leaving a notification-preemption race in this PR's own path.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| 1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | crates/daemon/src/idle_nudge.rs | 278-301 | Shared occurrence is disclosed by the earlier holder nudge, allowing reservation of a later prime FYI ID before admission | 9/10 |

## S189-001, remaining occurrence-disclosure race

The holder nudge uses `idle-nudge:<seat>:<anchor>:<occurrence>`. `nudge` awaits its admission before resolving primes and holding each `idle-nudge-fyi:<seat>:<anchor>:<occurrence>:<prime>`. All these identifiers reuse the same 16-byte random value.

On ordinary new-message admission, delivery publishes `message.pushed` and `delivery.outcome` before returning the receipt (`delivery/mod.rs:1453-1488`). The outcome's metadata contains the complete message ID (`delivery/mod.rs:2503-2526`). For a cold holder, the forced-wake audit also publishes the full ID before admission (`pa_watchdog.rs:323-364,397-411`).

`GET /v1/events` gives an admitted local machine-key caller a live `EventFilter::all()` subscription, without a recipient filter (`http/mod.rs:3972-4075`). The attack therefore needs only message-ID metadata, not victim message bodies, token theft, victim identity assertion or daemon-sender impersonation.

An allowed interleaving is:

1. The daemon commits the stretch mark and publishes the holder nudge's occurrence-bearing ID.
2. An ordinary local event subscriber obtains the occurrence from that metadata and derives the future prime FYI ID using public seat/prime/anchor facts.
3. Before the later prime hold obtains its write/publication turn, the caller holds that exact ID as itself for a valid recipient through the existing FYI send path (`http/shim.rs:799-813`).
4. The daemon's prime hold now correctly refuses and audits `E-RS-FYI-ID-TAKEN`; no prime FYI is stored. The committed stretch mark still prevents a retry.

Event publication serializes each individual commit and broadcast, not the entire nudge/prime fanout (`events/mod.rs:131-158`). The intervening awaits and independent admission tasks leave this interleaving possible. Successful runtime exploitation was not attempted; this is a source-confirmed race, not a claim that every subscriber wins it.

Moving FYIs ahead of the holder nudge alone is insufficient for multiple primes: the first `fyi.held` event exposes its ID (`core/src/fyi.rs:239-253`) before the next prime hold, still revealing their shared occurrence.

Give each prime FYI an independent unpredictable ID, also independent of the holder nudge, and preserve the fail-before-mark behavior. Alternatively, admit the entire protected fanout atomically before exposing any identifier that determines an unadmitted sibling. The regression must cover disclosure/interleaving, not only preholding the old predictable ID.

PM agreed this remaining path belongs in #189 and requested this exact-head finding while its repair is prepared.

## Repairs and scope

`SqliteQueue::hold_fyi` reads the conflicting `(origin,id)` row inside the same owned write transaction. A different sender **or** recipient appends `fyi.refused` and commits no new FYI; audit/write failure propagates instead of becoming Held (`store/src/queue.rs:1205-1264`). Delivery observes that event and returns the new failure (`delivery/mod.rs:819-840`). Same-sender/same-recipient retries preserve the original FYI rather than replacing it. The fake mirrors those functional outcomes, not an independent concurrency proof.

`getrandom::fill` supplies 16 bytes and fails before the stretch mark. The conditional mark now rechecks live/idle state and absence of a newer own event under the store writer. Parameterized index queries and existing closed label rendering do not introduce new shell execution, identity authority or changed-line C19/C21 disclosure.

The newly added audit fields are structured JSON metadata, not raw text inserted into a daemon-authored instruction. Arbitrary data remains untrusted.

The other six FYI notice families now benefit from generic conflicting-row refusal/audit, but their predictable identifiers can still be occupied to prevent delivery. Normal-message `accept` identities are unchanged and are not protected by this FYI check. Those preexisting namespace problems can remain in the proposed F141; no blanket clearance of their per-site consequences is claimed. This block requires the #189-specific shared-occurrence race to be fixed here, not unrelated notification rewrites.

Prior full-label cross-project fanout and mark-before-send/cancellation qualifications remain. This head does not add project-isolated label disclosure or durable retry after a spent mark.

## CI evidence

Worktree is clean; local HEAD, remote branch and GitHub head agree; PR is CLEAN. CI [42491302475](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42491302475) succeeded. Checkout logs identify synthetic merge `9b058b5`, containing this exact head and main `9c3445c2`.

JUnit artifact [13621611596](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42491302475/artifacts/13621611596) was uploaded by the successful rust-test job and contains 2,247 passing cases, no failures; the runner separately reports five skipped. The old-ID collision regression, three-way stretch-veto regression, snapshot-busy guard, once-per-stretch/restart and designated-prime cases executed successfully. The collision test preholds only the old ID and does not interleave a reservation after disclosure of the new occurrence.

Both Node checks, Rust lint/test and the current Delivers check are green; one superseded Delivers run was cancelled. Fourteen mutant kills are author evidence, not independently rerun mutations.

No local builds/tests, exploit or live-system probes, credential reads or product edits. The review helper returned no assessment; this verdict rests on direct static inspection and GitHub CI, not a second-model approval.
